decision: Use Nginx and FastAPI in one application container. Nginx terminates TLS, serves the compiled React application, applies HTTP limits and security headers, and proxies /api to FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8000.

alternatives.name: Uvicorn/FastAPI handles TLS, React files and API

assessment.tls: Supported directly, but certificate reload requires process restart and application ownership of TLS settings.
assessment.certificate_renewal: Container restart or application-specific reload procedure.
assessment.upload_limits: Requires ASGI middleware or request-stream enforcement before multipart parsing.
assessment.timeouts: Uvicorn exposes keep-alive and graceful-shutdown timeouts, but request-body and upstream-style policies require application code or another component.
assessment.static_files: FastAPI/Starlette can serve them, but cache policy and SPA fallback become application concerns.
assessment.logs: Single process, but access and application concerns share configuration.
assessment.diagnostic: One process, but more HTTP-edge behavior is custom code.
assessment.docker_complexity: One process and no Nginx configuration; additional application middleware and tests are required.

alternatives.name: Nginx and FastAPI in the same container

assessment.tls: Nginx owns the HTTPS edge using mature SSL directives.
assessment.certificate_renewal: A container restart is the canonical Portainer procedure; Nginx can also reload certificates without changing application code if later required.
assessment.upload_limits: client_max_body_size and client_body_timeout reject requests at the HTTP edge before FastAPI multipart handling.
assessment.timeouts: Nginx owns client and proxy timeouts declaratively.
assessment.security_headers: Central declarative headers at the edge.
assessment.static_files: Nginx serves immutable Vite assets efficiently with explicit cache rules and SPA fallback.
assessment.logs: Nginx access/error logs and FastAPI application logs remain distinct on stdout/stderr.
assessment.healthcheck: Nginx /healthz verifies the edge while proxying /api/health verifies FastAPI; the container healthcheck uses the edge.
assessment.diagnostic: Two process logs, but clear separation between HTTP edge and business application.
assessment.docker_complexity: Two processes in one container and a small PID 1 entrypoint; still one Portainer service, image, volume and compose file.

rationale: The target optimizes maintainability and reinstallability, not process count.
Variant A would move reverse-proxy responsibilities into custom ASGI middleware and application tests.
Variant B keeps those policies declarative while preserving one image, one service, one container and one compose.yml.
No third-party process supervisor is required: the entrypoint starts both processes, traps TERM/INT, and exits if either child exits.
constraints: FastAPI listens only on 127.0.0.1 inside the container.
Node and Vite exist only in the frontend build stage.
Certificate files are mounted read-only and are never included in Git or the image.
Portainer Git Stack remains the only deployment and lifecycle interface.
Certificate replacement is completed through a Portainer redeploy for the V2 foundation.
